mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the partnership agreement (contrat de société) for the SCSp; if privately executed, a notarially certified extract is recommended
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the country of incorporation or domestic notary in country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Valid passport copy of the general partner (associé gérant) and all beneficial owners holding ≥25%
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority or notary in country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of registered address of the general partner (if a legal entity) or residence of natural persons
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Municipal registry or utility authority in country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) SDN list, United Nations Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, Smartmatic Luxembourg FIU directives, and national politically exposed persons (PEP) databases. Enhanced due diligence required for any PEP, high-risk jurisdiction, or sanctioned intermediary; results must be documented and retained for a minimum of five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (lbr.lu) - Company Name Reservation Portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be submitted in French, German, English, or Luxembourgish; if using a foreign script, a Latin-character transliteration is mandatory. The name must be distinctive, lawful, and not contrary to public policy or accepted moral standards.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file a written appeal with the Registrar of the Luxembourg Business Registers within 15 days. If the administrative appeal is dismissed, a judicial appeal must be lodged before the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement) within two months of the final administrative decision, citing the grounds of infringement of statutory naming criteria.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For an unregulated SCSp operating a voice streaming application, a virtual office is accepted only if the registered address is equipped for the receipt of legal correspondence and statutory notifications; however, commercial substance such as decision-making management and core operations must be demonstrable in Luxembourg. A physical presence or a service provider with physical premises is strongly recommended.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk of unannounced physical on-site inspections: 15% for digital service providers without physical presence; risk escalates above 30% if money laundering indicators, suspicious transaction reports, or material deviations from declared substance are identified.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended by the Law of 23 July 2016 introducing the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp), Articles 111-1 et seq.; Law of 19 December 2002 on the Trade and Companies Register (RCS) and the electronic companies bulletin (Recueil Électronique des Sociétés); Law of 13 January 2019 on the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés), maintained at the District Court of Luxembourg City.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Registration application for the Trade and Companies Register together with the executed partnership agreement (contrat de société) filed electronically, followed by publication in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés (RES).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: SCSp has no minimum statutory capital, no mandatory paid-up capital and no escrow or blocked-account requirement under Luxembourg law. The partnership agreement (contrat de société) freely determines the partners' contributions, which may be in cash, in kind, or as a contribution promise.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the General Partner of LU_SCSP (the "Partnership") hereby accepts the subscription of capital contributions by the initial limited partner in accordance with the partnership agreement. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Partnership be established at 12 Rue de l'École de Droit, L-1531 Luxembourg, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name] be and is hereby appointed as manager of the Partnership with full power to execute the registration filing with the Luxembourg Business Registers, open bank accounts, and appoint professional advisers. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the General Partner is authorized to enter into all agreements necessary to commence the interactive voice streaming social application business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Availability Check and Reservation with the LBR
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - online eServices portal (lbr.lu)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an interactive name search in the RCS database and file an online application for reservation of the proposed corporate name. Ensure the name is distinctive and does not conflict with existing RCS registrations or protected trade names. Engage Luxembourg corporate counsel or a notary to authenticate the reservation where required.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate names (up to three alternatives)
Certified passport copy of the general partner
Power of attorney if filed by a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused on grounds of similarity or public order, immediately reserve the first available alternative name or file a written objection with the LBR within the statutory response window; resubmission is available instantly through the eServices portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Authentication of the Partnership Agreement (Contrat de Société)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (optional) / qualified Luxembourg corporate counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the partnership agreement either by private writing under private signature or by notarial deed. The agreement must set out the corporate name, registered office, purpose, identity of the general and limited partners, capital contributions, profit-sharing arrangements, and management powers. Where the SCSp business is entirely digital and involves no contribution of real property, a private writing suffices; arrange apostille or legalization for signatures executed outside Luxembourg.
required_dossiers: Draft partnership agreement (contrat de société)
Certified passport copies of all partners
Proof of residential or corporate address of the general partner
Bank reference letter for each contributing partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If execution is formally defective, remedy by executing a rectification deed (acte rectificatif) before the same notary or by obtaining fresh private signatures; the corrected deed is then refiled with the RCS.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the Registration Application with the Trade and Companies Register (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - RCS eServices or Registry of the District Court of Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed partnership agreement together with the electronic registration application. Pay the applicable filing fee, obtain the RCS registration number (numéro d'immatriculation), and request publication in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés (RES). The manager or an authorized professional must certify the conformity of the filed copy with the original deed.
required_dossiers: Executed partnership agreement (certified copy)
RCS registration application form
Consent of the general partner and of the appointed manager
Certified identity documents of the general partner and manager
Proof of registered office address in Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS registrar issues a query or formal requisition, cure within fifteen days by submitting the supplementary declaration or document; if registration is refused, convene the general partner, amend the partnership agreement, and resubmit the complete dossier.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) and Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Transmit the RCS extract and partnership agreement to the ACD to obtain the Luxembourg tax identification number. Register with the AEDT for Luxembourg VAT purposes, which applies to subscription fees and in-app purchases made through the voice streaming application. If the operator is non-EU, appoint a Luxembourg tax representative and file the appropriate VAT registration forms.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
Executed partnership agreement
Proof of registered office address
Identity documents of the general partner and manager
Commercial description of the voice streaming application and payment rails
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax identification number is delayed, send a written follow-up to the ACD under the tax procedure rules; if the VAT registration is queried, clarify the intermediary classification of Apple IAP and Google Play Billing and submit the platform agreement as supplementary evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the Bank Account and Deposit of Capital Contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution selected by the manager (subject to the Law of 12 November 2004 on anti-money laundering)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a Luxembourg resident bank account in the name of the SCSp. Complete full know-your-customer and beneficial-owner due diligence, provide the executed partnership agreement and RCS extract, and deposit the agreed initial contribution. No statutory minimum deposit applies, but the manager should obtain a certificate of deposit for the partnership records.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
Executed partnership agreement
Certified passport copies of all signatories
Beneficial owner identification and source-of-funds documentation
Commercial description of the voice streaming business
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests enhanced due diligence, provide notarially certified source-of-wealth evidence and an updated ownership chart; escalate any unresolved request to the bank's compliance officer through the account relationship manager.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Beneficial Owner Declaration and Governance File Completion
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) - Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the beneficial owner declaration identifying all natural persons who own or control the SCSp within the statutory deadline. Convene the initial management meeting, record the first management minutes, and retain at the registered office the partners' register, the adopted resolutions, the partnership agreement, and the RCS and VAT certificates.
required_dossiers: Beneficial owner declaration form
Ownership and control organizational chart
Copy of the initial board resolution
RCS registration extract
VAT registration certificate (if obtained)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late filing of the RBE declaration exposes the SCSp to administrative fines; the cure is immediate online filing through the LBR portal and payment of any applicable late fee, followed by updating the declaration upon any change of partners.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - Ministry of the Economy (Ministère de l'Économie); no industrial establishment authorization under the Law of 30 April 2004 on commercial establishments is engaged by a data-only interactive audio and voice streaming software publisher.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable - the voice streaming application is an unregulated digital service; an 'autorisation d'établissement' under the Law of 2 September 2011 would only become mandatory upon the opening of a physical commercial or handicraft establishment in Luxembourg.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement - Luxembourg Environment Agency
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt (no formal EIA); the registered office is a non-industrial office use under the Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment, and no screening decision is required for a data-only software activity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to the digital service itself; general compliance with the EU Waste Framework Directive (2008/98/EC) and WEEE/RoHS restrictions if any physical devices are distributed; office waste must be handled by authorized municipal collection services.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Office-use clearance: obtain a fire safety certificate pursuant to the Grand-Ducal regulation on fire protection for the registered office, verify workplace health and safety compliance with the Luxembourg Labour Code (Code du travail), and secure an inspection clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM). No industrial structural-load inspection or special civil-defense permit applies to a software-only office occupation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) — Luxembourg Direct Tax Authority; registration portal: MyGuichet.lu (official e-Government platform for tax and business registration).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities must appoint a Luxembourg resident authorized representative or tax agent, file the incorporation/registration form with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) via MyGuichet.lu, obtain a Luxembourg business registration number (matricule), and then register with the Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for the national tax identification number (NIF). The ACD issues a permanent tax ID following submission of the notarized deed, partnership agreement, proof of registered office, and identification of partners/managers. In addition, the entity must register for VAT with the Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) if taxable activities commence in Luxembourg or if distance sales/electronic services to Luxembourg consumers exceed the applicable registration threshold.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The SCSp is fiscally transparent by default for Luxembourg corporate income tax purposes; no check-the-box election is required to establish pass-through treatment. The partnership agreement and the allocation of profits and voting rights determine the partners' deemed Luxembourg establishment status. However, if a partner is a Luxembourg-resident corporate entity subject to CIT, its share of SCSp income remains taxable at the partner level. No hybrid mismatch election is available to alter the fiscal transparency of an SCSp, although Luxembourg applies controlled foreign company and anti-hybrid rules consistent with EU ATAD as implemented in the Luxembourg domestic code. Parties may structure the SCSp as either a commercial or non-commercial partnership, which affects whether it is subject to Luxembourg municipal business tax (commune trade tax) at partnership level for business activity; if the SCSp carries on a commercial undertaking and has a permanent establishment deemed to exist via the general partner, it falls within the scope of the municipal business tax, with tax transparency for CIT purposes preserved.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée — TVA), under Luxembourg VAT law (Loi TVA) and EU VAT Directive as implemented.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual turnover for Luxembourg-resident businesses in certain low-value supplies; for foreign suppliers of telecommunications, broadcasting, and electronic services (including voice streaming apps sold to non-taxable persons within Luxembourg), no general registration threshold applies beyond the EU cross-border threshold of EUR 10,000 for intra-Community distance sales if the supplier is established in another EU Member State; non-EU suppliers have no threshold and must register or use the OSS for non-EU supplier registration for EU B2C electronic services. For Luxembourg domestic and other supplies, the mandatory registration threshold for established businesses is EUR 35,000 (for small business exemption); otherwise registration is obligatory irrespective of turnover once taxable supplies commence.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg has not mandated a real-time transaction clearance or continuous transaction control (CTC) system as of the knowledge cutoff. Luxembourg's B2B domestic e-invoicing is not compulsory on a national basis; however, e-invoices must be accepted where the recipient agrees, and since 2019, Luxembourg permits the exchange of electronic invoices that comply with the EU e-invoicing standard (EN 16931) under the PEPPOL network for public procurement. Luxembourg has implemented the EU cross-border e-invoicing obligation for supplies to Luxembourg public authorities via the B2G platform, using PEPPOL. There is no general API-based real-time fiscal stamping requirement for private-sector e-invoicing. All businesses must maintain authentic VAT invoices with required fields, and for digital services, invoices should identify the service and VAT treatment.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to goods dispatched to non-EU destinations and to certain supplies of services connected with export (e.g., freight and related services, plus supplies of digital or electronically supplied services may be not zero-rated but rather taxed at the place of the customer if B2C; zero-rating for export goods is available only for direct exports of movable goods where the goods physically leave the EU customs territory. For the voice streaming app, if the service is provided to a non-EU business customer outside the EU, Luxembourg VAT rules and EU B2B place-of-supply rules treat the supply as outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT (no Luxembourg VAT) if the customer is established outside the EU; if provided to non-EU private consumers, the place of supply remains the customer's residence (not Luxembourg), so no Luxembourg VAT applies, but this is not technically an export zero-rating claim; instead the supply falls outside the territorial scope of Luxembourg VAT. For tangible exports, zero-rating is subject to providing transport documents proving exit from the EU and the customs export declaration.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (formal customs acceptance/export accompanying document under EU Union Customs Code, with MRN and exit confirmation from the customs office of exit)
Bill of Lading or other transport document (airway bill, road consignment note, or shipping evidence) evidencing physical departure of goods from EU territory)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank/credit institution payment proof showing the export proceeds transferred in foreign currency and received in Luxembourg or partner bank account)
Commercial invoice and order documentation matching the customs declaration and evidencing the service or goods supply
Supplier's VAT registration certificate and, where applicable, partner's foreign tax certificate supporting non-established customer status
Audit trail of digital service provision logs, IP location data, and customer records for offshore services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Substantiation penalties: unfounded or excessive VAT refunds or zero-rating claims are subject to recovery of underpaid VAT, interest at the statutory rate, and administrative fines up to EUR 4,000 per infringement, plus criminal penalties in cases of fraud or material concealment (prison sentence and monetary penalty up to EUR 15,000 for fraud under Article 92 of the Luxembourg VAT law). Retrospective clawback: the Luxembourg AEDT may reassess VAT for up to five years (extended to ten years in cases of fraud) and claw back zero-rated/VAT-free treatment with a 10% to 20% penalty alongside interest for late payment; fraudulent export zero-rating schemes are prosecuted under general criminal law and the VAT fraud provisions, with exposure to joint and several liability of directors and partners and potential loss of the right to deduct input VAT.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) as the national central bank within the Eurosystem, supported by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for banking conduct, AML/CFT and payment-services supervision. Luxembourg has no separate foreign-exchange administration and BCL assumes external-statistics oversight.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is the sole legal tender; Luxembourg applies unrestricted convertibility on both current and capital accounts under Article 63 TFEU and the EU free-movement-of-capital regime, and no approval is required for profit remittance, distributions, or capital repatriation. For the SCSp, which is tax-transparent, partnership profit allocations to non-resident limited partners are not subject to currency-conversion licensing or Luxembourg withholding at allocation. Practical remittance constraints are limited to: (i) BCL external-statistics reporting obligations when flows exceed prescribed de minimis thresholds; (ii) funds-transfer information requirements under Regulation (EU) 2015/847; and (iii) the requirement that all end-user payments be routed solely through Apple IAP and Google Play Billing, thereby avoiding the creation of an unlicensed payment institution under the Luxembourg Law of 10 November 2009 on payment services.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No export-proceeds surrender rules, mandatory conversion ratios, or repatriation deadlines exist in Luxembourg law. App-store collections of digital service export proceeds may be held in foreign currency indefinitely. The only administrative duties are BCL balance-of-payments external-statistics filings, which may require monthly, quarterly, or annual reporting depending on transaction volumes and counterparty residency, plus normal VAT and Intrastat declarations applicable to intra-EU digital services; neither imposes any FX surrender or conversion requirement.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium, for ancillary treasury operations only, not as a primary clearing rail. A European Economic Area electronic-money institution passported into Luxembourg under PSD2 (e.g., Wise Europe, Revolut Business, N26 Business) or a CSSF-licensed Luxembourg EMI may be opened for low-value SEPA payroll, vendor disbursements, and small multi-currency payments; however, EMIs are not credit institutions and cannot support capital escrow, commercial letters of credit, SWIFT-gpi MT103 clearing for large settlements, or structured FX lines. Non-EEA EMIs (United Kingdom, United States, Hong Kong) are legally unable to provide euro-denominated account services without an EEA partner and should not be used for the SCSp's registered treasury relationship; their use would also raise enhanced-review concerns under CSSF Regulation 12-02 because limited partners would be exposed to an unregulated custodian of float.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Given the Medium_Risk_Enhanced classification applicable to the interactive voice-streaming business, Tier-1 Luxembourg banks require at least one physical presence onboarding and an in-person KYC interview of one authorised signatory who is either a Luxembourg-resident manager or an ultimate beneficial owner. The general partner and any remaining directors may complete the process remotely through a hybrid video-plus-certified-documents procedure, provided that a Luxembourg notary or a regulated professional support professional (PSF) attests the identity documents under CSSF Regulation 12-02. Fully remote onboarding is considered only when the SCSp presents a clean RBE certificate, a professional-intermediary attestation, and evidence of a long-term Luxembourg substance arrangement; in practice, the principal bank relationship commences with a physical interview at the bank's Luxembourg offices.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp pass-through structure with undisclosed limited partners, creating ambiguity as to ultimate beneficial ownership and control.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Updated RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) extract showing the complete natural-person ownership chain; limited partnership agreement and latest capitalization table; capital call notices and subscription agreements for every limited partner; an ownership/control diagram mapping the general partner to its ultimate beneficial owners; a notarized Luxembourg deed confirming the appointment of the general partner and its authority; and a Luxembourg counsel legal opinion confirming the transparency of the SCSp for AML purposes and that no silent partner holds veto rights without disclosure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity micro-transactions, virtual gifting, tips and in-app digital-currency flows that may be perceived as unlicensed payment aggregation or money-laundering vectors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apple Developer Program License Agreement and Google Play Developer Distribution Agreement; last twelve months of app-store payout reports demonstrating that funds reach the SCSp only after platform commission deduction; an in-app virtual-currency whitepaper proving one-way purchase economics with no user-to-user fiat conversion, no wallet withdrawal, and no cash-back; platform refund, chargeback and dispute-resolution policies; automated transaction-velocity and anti-fraud monitoring rules; KYC/AML documentation for high-volume streamers and gift receivers exceeding platform risk thresholds; and a source-to-settlement transaction-flow diagram showing that zero end-user payments are received directly into the SCSp bank account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated entity without operating history or demonstrable Luxembourg substance, raising promoter and business-continuity concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: RCS (Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register) extract dated within one month; registered office lease agreement or Luxembourg substance-service-provider agreement; Luxembourg VAT (TVA) registration certificate and employer registration documentation if any; three-year financial forecast and capital deployment plan; evidence that minimum committed capital is held in the dedicated capital escrow account; financial statements for any predecessor operating company, if applicable; and a statement of Luxembourg substance KPIs covering local board seat, decision-making records, domain name, bank account and invoicing infrastructure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital contributions originating from non-EU, high-risk or material-wealth jurisdictions, including partners whose wealth traces to digital-asset appreciation, creating elevated source-of-funds exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A structured source-of-wealth and source-of-funds file per non-EU limited partner: regulated-bank reference letters, audited financial statements or accountant-verified net-worth statements, recent tax assessments or wealth-tax returns, and acquisition/exit documentation supporting the origin of contributed funds; signed adherence to the bank's no-third-party-funding clause; negative media, sanctions and PEP screening results for each partner and its beneficial owners; an affirmation from the general partner that no funds originate from sanctioned persons or unlicensed virtual-asset intermediaries; and legalization or apostille of corporate documents under the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Risk that the platform, by enabling digital gifting or virtual credits through app stores, is seen as performing payment services or issuing e-money without a Luxembourg CSSF licence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A legal-engineering pack containing a Luxembourg-law opinion analyzing the scope exemption from the Law of 10 November 2009 on payment services; contractual design confirming that the mobile applications act only as storefronts and that settlement of net proceeds is made by Apple/Google to the SCSp in its capacity as merchant, not as payment service provider; the platform's standard terms of service prohibiting withdrawal, conversion or transfer of virtual coins to fiat currency; a data-flow and settlement diagram; a negative declaration filed with the CSSF or a statement from counsel confirming that no authorisation is required; and a complaint/whistle-blower register demonstrating operational compliance.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound contributions are executed exclusively via SWIFT MT103 or higher-value real-time TARGET2 transfers from each limited partner's regulated bank account to the SCSp's Capital Escrow Account. Standard protocol: (1) the general partner issues a capital call notice carrying a unique reference and the exact amount; (2) the partner instructs its bank with structured remittance data including the SCSp legal name, capital call reference, partner legal name, and BCL external-statistics classification of the transfer as a direct-investment equity contribution; (3) the Luxembourg receiving bank performs sanctions screening and verifies that the originator account name exactly matches the limited partner in the subscription agreement; (4) upon matching of reference and amount, funds are credited to the segregated escrow account and a drawdown certificate signed by the general partner releases them to the operational account; and (5) every monthly cycle the BCL external-statistics report records the liability to non-resident partners under the direct-investment heading. For euro-denominated partner capital exceeding EUR 500,000 or for same-day deployment, TARGET2 is strongly preferred; all confirmations must preserve the UETR (Unique End-to-End Transaction Reference) to satisfy Regulation (EU) 2015/847 information requirements.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The primary clearing rails are SEPA Credit Transfer and SEPA Instant for euro disbursements within the EEA, and SWIFT MT103/MT202 with GPI end-to-end tracking for non-euro and non-EEA settlements. For high-value licensing agreements covering music rights, voice-AI models, or influencer streaming contracts, the disbursement structure may incorporate a sight Commercial Letter of Credit opened by the SCSp's bank, or a standby letter of credit when the counterparty requires a bank payment guarantee; documents are presented electronically under eUCP 2.0 where applicable. App-store proceeds (Apple IAP and Google Play Billing) are collected through Apple Distribution International and Google Ireland payout rails, settled in EUR, and concentrated into the operational account via a daily automatic sweep; any USD, GBP, JPY or KRW receipts are converted through a standing monthly FX contract rather than spot conversions. The treasury function maintains a daily liquidity calendar covering contractual payment dates, payroll, VAT accruals, partner distributions, and prudential buffer targets, with liquidity forecasting managed through the bank's electronic-banking ISO 20022 CAMT reporting.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright over-the-counter FX forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP) exceeding one-week tenor, documented under an ISDA 1998 FX Master Agreement or the FX Global Code framework, with hedging intent evidenced by app-store revenue forecasts
FX swaps (rollovers) for short-term treasury liquidity management of up to three months, executed at the same Luxembourg credit institution

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for EUR/CNH and EUR/KRW, permitted to hedge app-store or in-app revenue streams settled in non-convertible or restricted currencies and cleared offshore through the bank's NDF desk
Zero-premium FX option collars (put/call combinations) on EUR/USD to protect the annual partner-distribution conversion budget while allowing upside participation within a defined band

Cross-currency interest rate swaps only when the SCSp maintains a foreign-currency (USD or GBP) partner loan or treasury line, and solely to convert that exposure into EUR, never for speculative purposes

Regulatory overlay governing all instruments: trades must be executed under a CRD/CSDR-compliant counterparty with an ISDA CSA or credit support annex, reported at trade, valuation and confirmation level to an EU-authorised trade repository under EMIR (Regulation (EU) 648/2012), and cleared through a qualifying CCP if the SCSp crosses the NFC-plus clearing thresholds; a commercial documentation register must demonstrate that all hedging is connected to underlying commercial contracts and does not expose the pass-through partners to unmanaged speculative gains

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (comptes annuels) filed with the Luxembourg Business Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Register (RCS - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of the financial year-end (e.g., 30 June for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of up to €250 per day capped at €7,500, court-imposed fines up to €25,000, and potential administrative strike-off after repeated non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO Register Confirmation and Notification of Any Beneficial Ownership Changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Not a static annual filing; update within 30 days of any transfer of partnership interests or move of registered office. Confirm accuracy on the annual anniversary during the annual accounts board-meeting review.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to €1,250 per non-compliance, and criminal penalties for false declarations up to €25,000 and/or imprisonment.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: SCSp must undergo a mandatory independent audit by a Luxembourg approved statutory auditor ('réviseur d'entreprises agréé') if it exceeds two of the three following size criteria on two consecutive balance sheet dates: total balance sheet €4.4 million; net turnover €8.8 million; average number of employees 50. Solely for tax transparency, no audit is required if the entity falls below these thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP pursuant to the Luxembourg Law of 19 December 2020 on the register of commercial companies (Loi du 19 décembre 2020) and the Law on Commercial Companies (LSC). IFRS may be applied voluntarily but is not mandatory for an SCSp.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp is a tax-transparent partnership; any transfer of partnership interests or change in beneficial ownership triggers an immediate RBE update (within 30 days). No separate yearly UBO declaration is required; however, the registered agent must verify and confirm the register's accuracy at each annual general meeting or within the preparation of the annual accounts, whichever occurs first.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (Luxembourg City 2025 aggregate nominal rate: 17.00% corporate income tax + 7.00% solidarity surcharge on the CIT + 6.75% municipal business tax on trading profit). The SCSp is itself exempt from entity-level CIT because, under Article 185 LIR and the law of 12 July 2013, the SCSp is fiscally transparent: its net income is allocated directly to partners in accordance with the partnership agreement and taxed only in the hands of those partners; non-resident partners without a Luxembourg permanent establishment are not taxed in Luxembourg on their allocated share.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Full pass-through with no entity-level CIT, net wealth tax or dividend WHT at the SCSp level; Luxembourg participation exemption allowing 100% exemption of qualifying dividends and capital gains (10% shareholding or EUR 1,200,000 acquisition cost, 12-month holding period, substance and holding purpose conditions); EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief for qualifying EU corporate partners; zero statutory WHT on outbound royalties and interest; treaty benefits available to partners through look-through treatment where the partner provides a valid tax residency certificate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 710G informational return (déclaration de renseignements for sociétés de personnes) together with the partnership annex to Form 710 (corporate income tax and net wealth tax return). Filing is performed electronically through the eCDF (Electronic Communication and Data Filling) portal of the Administration des contributions directes via MyGuichet; partners file their own resident or non-resident returns separately.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The SCSp information return must be filed by 31 December of the calendar year following the fiscal year-end (for a calendar-year SCSp, the FY2024 return is due by 31 December 2025). A filing extension to 30 June of the following year is routinely granted where an approved tax professional files electronically; the tax administration may further extend the deadline upon reasoned request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full legal name of the SCSp, RCS Luxembourg registration number, registered office address, RBE (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) registration reference and the name of the gérant (general partner) acting as filing representative.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The gérant files on behalf of the non-resident partners; no local tax number is required for partners unless they have a Luxembourg PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Accounting period and closing figures
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening and closing book dates, balance sheet total, and the net accounting profit or loss before partner allocation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report in EUR; translate foreign-currency income using the official ECB exchange rate of the closing accounting date; no Luxembourg reclassification for partners without PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Profit and loss allocation schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule allocating the accounting result to each partner with exact percentages, contributed capital, profit shares and any carried interest, per the SCSp limited partnership agreement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide each partner's name, country of tax residence, treaty country, share percentage and the allocated profit/loss amount; this schedule drives the look-through taxation and must be reconciled with the investor register.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible expenses (fines, fictional interest, excessive remuneration, 50% of entertainment costs), depreciation recapture, tax-exempt items, and carried losses claimed under the 17-year carryforward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners with no Luxembourg PE should state nil in this box; any Luxembourg-source add-backs are only relevant where the partner has a deemed local presence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of intragroup flows: App Store/Google Play licensing income, technical service fees, intercompany loans, cost-sharing agreements, content moderation charges and any royalty flows to or from connected parties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This box must cross-reference the OECD-conform Local File; for non-resident partners, cross-reference the group Master File and confirm that the arm's-length net margin is substantiated by a benchmark study.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Treaty relief and foreign tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of foreign-source income (e.g., China-sourced streaming royalties), foreign taxes borne, and any DTA relief requested on behalf of the partners.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach valid tax residence certificates for each partner claiming treaty relief; include beneficial ownership declarations; refund claims must be lodged within the 5-year statutory window.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Unfiled or late returns trigger default assessment (imposition d'office) with rejection of unproven deductions, a late-filing surcharge of up to 10% of the assessed tax, monthly late-payment interest at 0.6% on the outstanding amount, and coercive administrative fines of up to EUR 5,000 for repeated non-compliance; in fraud cases the assessment window extends to 10 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory dividend withholding tax for distributions by fully taxable Luxembourg resident companies. The transparent SCSp is not a withholding agent: distributions to its partners are look-through in nature, the character of the underlying income is preserved, and no Luxembourg WHT is charged at the partnership level. If the SCSp has opted for taxable status or is treated as an opaque entity in the partner's jurisdiction, distributions may be requalified and exposed to 15% WHT unless reduced under a treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Step 1: the partner obtains a current tax residence certificate (TRC) from its fiscal authority and completes the Luxembourg 'beneficial owner' declaration; Step 2: the payer (Luxembourg operating subsidiary or the SCSp if opaque) applies the treaty rate at source upon receipt of the TRC, e.g., 5% on dividends for a 10% or greater shareholding under the Luxembourg-People's Republic of China DTA, or 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for EU corporate partners holding at least 10% for 12 months; Step 3: where excess WHT was retained, the partner files a refund claim with the Administration des contributions directes within 5 years; Step 4: retain the TRC, allocation schedules and underlying accounting records for at least 10 years to withstand a look-through audit.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg imposes no source WHT on outbound royalties or debt interest: the statutory rate is 0% for both. Inbound, the counterparty source state may levy its domestic WHT (e.g., the Luxembourg-PRC DTA provides 10% on royalties and 10% on interest; the EU Interest and Royalties Directive cancels such WHT for EU group companies holding 25% or more for at least 24 months). The voice-streaming platform should therefore structure IP licensing so that the SCSp receives royalties net of source tax at the reduced treaty rate, with foreign tax credits flowing through to the partners.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Luxembourg law contains no codified monetary de-minimis; Circular LIR 56/1/5 of 10 April 2023 requires contemporaneous OECD-aligned Local File and Master File documentation whenever material cross-border related-party transactions exist. For this SCSp, prepare a full Local File from the first euro of intercompany royalty or service flow; the practical audit trigger is aggregate intra-group transaction value above EUR 1,000,000 per annum, and a Master File is expected when the consolidated group revenue exceeds EUR 50,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not apply Gulf-style Economic Substance Regulations, but economic substance is dispositive for tax transparency and treaty benefits: (a) Article 6 StAnpG (Steueranpassungsgesetz) disregards artificial arrangements lacking a valid business purpose; (b) the OECD Multilateral Instrument Principal Purpose Test denies DTA benefits to arrangements whose principal purpose is tax relief; (c) ATAD implementation (interest limitation rule, CFC rules and exit taxation) is fully in force; (d) the participation exemption requires genuine establishment and real economic activity of the underlying subsidiary. An SCSp operating a voice-streaming app must demonstrate physical presence in Luxembourg, actual decision-making by the gérant, substantive payroll and office costs proportionate to the revenue, a functioning Luxembourg bank account, and commercial substance behind the Apple IAP/Google Play Billing revenue flows; otherwise the tax administration may recharacterise the structure, assert a partner-level PE in Luxembourg and deny treaty relief on the app-store income.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Filing (Fraude Fiscale)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilfully under-declaring voice-streaming revenue collected via Apple IAP and Google Play Billing, concealing partner profit allocations, submitting falsified or incomplete Form 710G annexes, or backdating intercompany royalty agreements to reduce taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Articles 985-987 LIR and the Luxembourg Criminal Code: imprisonment from 1 month to 5 years and criminal fines of up to EUR 25,000 per tax period for natural persons, with multiplied fines for legal persons; the tax administration additionally applies the 10% late-filing surcharge, monthly late-payment interest at 0.6%, and reopens the assessment period for up to 10 years in evasion cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant and any de facto manager are jointly and severally liable without limitation for the SCSp's tax debts; personal assets are directly reachable, the criminal conviction triggers disqualification from corporate offices, and the enforcement authorities may impose provisional asset freezes and travel bans.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the SCSp with zero Luxembourg substance: no office, no staff, no governance minutes, all App-Store revenue immediately re-invoiced to a related low-tax entity at a sub-margin without contemporaneous TP documentation, with the sole purpose of exploiting the transparent SCSp to avoid source-state withholding.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Application of the Luxembourg GAAR (Article 6 StAnpG) and the MLI Principal Purpose Test: the SCSp is disregarded, income is re-attributed to a Luxembourg or partner-level PE, treaty exemptions are denied, the participation exemption is revoked, and the resultant assessment carries 24.94% aggregate CIT plus 0.6% monthly late interest and a 10% surcharge; the partner's home jurisdiction may pursue CFC re-attribution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner's unlimited liability exposes the individual's personal estate; civil restitution orders cover the unpaid tax, interest and penalties; in severe cross-border cases the courts can issue a professional ban and a travel restriction against the controlling shareholder.
